US-531 CLOSED + COMMITTED as 6c54a96 (Sprint 71 / V0.29.26, 2/6 done). NO TD-059 STALL -- gate ran synchronously in-loop, then COMMIT, then bookkeeping. NEXT: US-532 (Iris Option-B settings band) or US-536 (disposition-B revert, size S). Read the Atlas --disable-gpu RCA inbox item BEFORE US-536.

WHAT SHIPPED: POST /settings, the THIRD token-gated write route on states_http_server. Body {key, value}. It persists the US-530 overlay because the kiosk is sandboxed chromium JS and cannot write files.

I TOOK US-530'S HANDOFF LITERALLY AND IT PAID: ZERO new validation. The endpoint imports overlay.OVERRIDABLE_KEYS + validateOverlayValue, and the atomic write itself lives in common.config.overlay (writeOverlayValue), NOT in the HTTP layer -- same posture as US-403 delegating to service_control. The server stays a thin transport, and any future non-HTTP writer inherits the identical gate. If you are tempted to put validation in the handler: don't. Two gates that can disagree look stronger than one and are weaker.

*** THE LESSON: A HAPPY PATH CANNOT PROVE A RE-READ. *** The AC says return the REAL stored effective value, never an optimistic echo. My first suite only caught the echo on the FAILURE path -- because on a SUCCESSFUL write the stored value EQUALS the effective value, so an echoing endpoint passes every happy-path assertion. Narrow mutation (return `stored` but keep ok:wrote) -> only 1 red, which is how I found it. Fix: test_settingsWrite_storedButUnresolvable_reportsNullNotTheRequest -- a config.json whose pi.power branch is a STRING, so the write SUCCEEDS but the override cannot resolve onto it and the honest answer is null. GENERAL RULE: when a response is meant to be a RE-READ rather than an ECHO, you must construct a case where the stored value and the resolved value DISAGREE. This is the same family as US-530's 'never let the expected value equal the default'.

DECLARATION VS MECHANISM, AGAIN, THIRD SPRINT RUNNING. Under that mutation the WARNING log said 'Overlay key blocked by a non-dict branch' while the endpoint returned 'wall'. The log told the truth and the response lied. A log line is not a test.

MUTATIONS (all reverted BY HAND -- git checkout is outside the allow-list -- and re-verified green): (A) drop _tokenOk from the settings handler -> 2 red. (B) swap overlay.OVERRIDABLE_KEYS for an endpoint-local tuple missing one key -> red on the parametrized case. (C) echo the request -> 2 red.

HONEST BOUND ON (B): parametrizing over OVERRIDABLE_KEYS catches DRIFT, not duplication -- a local list currently IDENTICAL to the SSOT still passes. It fails the moment the allow-list grows, which is the real Slice-2 risk. I also assert the test's _VALID_VALUES map covers OVERRIDABLE_KEYS exactly, so a new overridable key cannot land untested.

ATOMICITY PINNED AS MECHANISM: a spy on os.replace asserts the destination IS the overlay path and the source is NOT -- a truncating open() of the live file would pass every other write test. Also proven: a failing replace leaves the prior overlay BYTE-IDENTICAL and leaves no .tmp behind. fsync before replace, because the Pi loses power with the ignition.

DELIBERATELY NO GET COUNTERPART. Effective values already reach the dashboard through the injected config (US-506 window.DISPLAY_CAROUSEL). A GET /settings would be a SECOND source for the same fact and could disagree with the injected one. US-532: render from the injected config, do NOT invent a read endpoint.

LEFT FOR US-533 ON PURPOSE: I did NOT bounce eclipse-states-http on an autoRotateS write. That is explicitly US-533's GAP-1 acceptance, and a service restart does not belong in a story scoped to persistence. The seam is ready (the handler knows the key it just wrote). Remember the carousel config is cached at states-http STARTUP -> auto-rotate needs a bounce + page reload and must be labeled 'applies on restart', NEVER claimed live.

REAL-CONFIG SMOKE beyond the fixtures: against the SHIPPED config.json, overlayPathFor -> config.local.json; authed writes 200 with real effective values; UNAUTHED write -> 401 AND the overlay still read the prior value afterwards (absence of a side effect, not merely a status code -- assert that, not just the code); pi.obd.port -> 403; config.json byte-unchanged. Artifact deleted, git status --ignored clean.

GATE: RED first for the right reason (ImportError: cannot import name 'getDotPath'). Then 346 passed, 1 skipped -- 2 story files + tests/common/test_config_overlay.py + all of tests/pi/splash/ + tests/test_secrets_loader.py. The 1 skip is PRE-EXISTING (test_token.py:70 POSIX file-mode on Windows). ruff clean on all 4 files; validate_config.py passes.

BLAST RADIUS FOR PM: a NEW WRITE SURFACE on the Pi -- worth the full suite at integration. Otherwise additive; every existing route untouched. I did switch states_http_server to `from common.config import overlay` (module import, needed for the monkeypatch seam) and grepped tests first to confirm nothing referenced the old bare `applyConfigOverlay` import.

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed): `make` is NOT on PATH -- `make lint` exits 127 which READS LIKE A PASS; use `python -m ruff check` per touched file (TD-075 keeps project-wide ruff at exit 1). NEW GOTCHA: the Bash tool REJECTS heredocs containing brace-with-quote (i.e. JSON object literals in inline python) as 'expansion obfuscation' -- build payloads with dict() instead of {"k": v}.
